newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen firm vs yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen firm vs yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to stay firm against the yen during Asian trading time on Wednesday after hitting a 56-month high of 126.52 yen in Europe, with few offers expected on the topside, dealers said.

Lingering concerns about possible Bank of Japan dollar-selling intervention may check the dollar's advance, but dealers say Japanese operators, such as institutional investors, are likely to remain keen to buy dollars on dips.
But a long-term credit bank dealer said profit-taking may emerge just below 127 yen, making it a bit difficult for the dollar to power its way above 127 yen during the Asian session.
"Buyers have become somewhat cautious at this level," she said, adding that if the dollar rises above the overnight high, it will continue to go up to near 127 yen.

The dollar hit 126.52 yen in Europe, its highest since August 1992, after Tsutomu Makino, Japan's Vice Trade Minister, said late on Tuesday that the weak yen was more positive than negative for the Japanese economy at the moment.

The dollar has risen more than four yen since last Friday, helped in part by a remark from U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that currencies should not be used as a tool to deal with Japan's trade surplus.
Dealers said the dollar has been bolstered by the widening interest rate gap between the United States and Japan.
In early Tokyo on Wednesday, U.S. trade expert Fred Bergsten sharply criticised Rubin for inconsistent trade and exchange rate policies towards Japan and called for action to stem the dollar rise.
He told Reuters Financial Television that the long-term dollar-yen equilibrium level would be 100-110 yen, adding that the dollar would continue to rise without some form of intervention.
His comments briefly weighed on the dollar.
Caution over the possibility of dollar sales intervention still remains in the market, which may weigh on the dollar, dealers said.
"I think Japanese authorities have become nervous lately," said a trust bank dealer.
